claim_text: Constructor theory proposes expressing fundamental laws through possible and impossible physical transformation tasks.
operational_terms: task; substrate; constructor; possible; impossible
specific_result_or_argument: A task is a set of input-output substrate transformations; possibility is defined by arbitrarily accurate constructors capable of repeated performance.
admissible_interventions: constructors allowed by the subsidiary theory
resource_bound: arbitrarily accurate repeatability; resources must be declared
assumptions: constructor-theoretic program and subsidiary physical theory
boundary_conditions: Declared substrates attributes accuracy standard and resources
alternative_interpretation: A reformulation of ordinary laws until it yields new theorems or tests
notes: Supports hard can/cannot language but not temporal inheritance by itself.

claim_text: Information media and variables can be characterized through the possible permutations copying and distinguishability tasks of physical substrates.
operational_terms: information medium; computation variable; cloning; distinguishability
specific_result_or_argument: The paper defines information attributes via task repertoires rather than taking information as an a priori abstraction.
admissible_interventions: copying permutations and distinguishing tasks
assumptions: constructor-theoretic principles including interoperability
boundary_conditions: Choice of attributes and subsidiary theory
alternative_interpretation: A physical task taxonomy rather than a new dynamical variable
notes: Useful embodiment criterion; does not identify the history that formed the medium.

claim_text: Constructor-based irreversibility is compatible with time-reversal-symmetric quantum laws in a universal-homogenizer model and is experimentally realizable in a photonic implementation.
operational_terms: possible task; impossible inverse; homogenizer; repeatability
page_or_section: Abstract; main model and experimental sections; figures reporting homogenizer implementation
specific_result_or_argument: The forward homogenizing task approaches reusable performance differently from its inverse; a single-photon implementation tests the model behavior.
predictive_interventional_or_counterfact: modal task claim with experimental implementation
admissible_interventions: specified homogenizer interactions and preparation/measurement operations
resource_bound: finite copies interactions and experimental error
assumptions: validity of homogenizer construction and mapping from finite experiment to constructor limit
boundary_conditions: Specific quantum model and photonic apparatus
alternative_interpretation: Evidence for one model's compatibility rather than for constructor theory as a universal framework
notes: Do not describe this as a universal experimental confirmation of constructor theory.

claim_text: A process tensor maps a sequence of admissible control operations to a future quantum state and hence to all measurement probabilities in the declared span.
operational_terms: process tensor; control sequence; Choi state; multi-time process
page_or_section: Sec. II pp. 2-3 Properties P1-P3 and Theorem 2; Sec. III Eqs. 8-12; Theorem 4
specific_result_or_argument: The framework is linear completely positive and satisfies containment; process tomography reconstructs the input-output law.
admissible_interventions: completely positive maps at declared time steps
resource_bound: finite time grid; tomography basis; possible MPO compression
assumptions: fixed system-environment partition and accessible control operations
boundary_conditions: Temporal resolution operation span and preparation assumptions
alternative_interpretation: A complete reduced input-output description without a unique microscopic record
notes: Closest quantum realization of the ICP intervention-indexed future family.

claim_text: Reduced process history dependence may be represented as memory carried by an environment and can disappear when the state boundary is enlarged.
operational_terms: unitary dilation; environment; memory; state augmentation
page_or_section: Sec. II dilation; pp. 8-9 MPO and environment-dimension discussion
specific_result_or_argument: Every process tensor admits a system-environment realization; the reduced process alone need not identify a unique carrier.
admissible_interventions: local CP maps on the designated system
resource_bound: depends on environment dimension and chosen boundary
assumptions: existence of a dilation does not imply unique microscopic realization
boundary_conditions: Chosen system boundary
alternative_interpretation: Ordinary enlarged-state dynamics explains apparent inherited memory
notes: Directly activates rival R002 and criterion F006.

claim_text: A causal-break intervention supplies a necessary and sufficient operational Markov condition for a quantum process.
operational_terms: causal break; measure-discard-reprepare; conditional future independence
page_or_section: p. 2 definition and Eqs. 1-2; pp. 3-4 factorization
specific_result_or_argument: After every causal break the future is independent of earlier controls and outcomes conditional on the reprepared state exactly when the process is operationally Markovian.
admissible_interventions: causal-break instruments and future instruments
resource_bound: finite temporal resolution and experimental operation set
assumptions: informationally adequate interventions on the selected system
boundary_conditions: System partition time grid and available instruments
alternative_interpretation: Memory is an operational property of a reduced description
notes: Provides a concrete design pattern for ICP carrier tests.

claim_text: Operational quantum memory is relative to the chosen system partition temporal resolution and accessible instruments.
operational_terms: partition; instrument set; memory size; falsifiability
page_or_section: pp. 3-4 Choi/MPO factorization and memory discussion
specific_result_or_argument: The test detects influences available through the declared interventions but does not make memory an observer-independent scalar or identify a unique carrier.
admissible_interventions: declared causal breaks and probes
assumptions: completeness only relative to the experimental setting
boundary_conditions: System-environment cut and accessible operation span
alternative_interpretation: A different partition or probe family may change the diagnosis
notes: ICP must carry Pi and the observable algebra in its definition.

claim_text: Non-Markovian finite quantum Markov order is generally instrument-specific; finite order for all instruments is essentially Markovian.
operational_terms: Markov order; memory instrument; conditional independence
specific_result_or_argument: History and future factorization can hold for one memory instrument and fail for another.
admissible_interventions: specified memory-block instruments
resource_bound: finite memory block and exact conditional factorization
assumptions: process-tensor formalism and declared instrument family
boundary_conditions: At least three temporal blocks; selected memory instrument
alternative_interpretation: There is no generally valid intervention-independent memory length
notes: Strong novelty boundary against intrinsic unindexed constraint states.

claim_text: Multi-time quantum processes form a strict hierarchy separating Markovian classical-memory and quantum-memory mechanisms.
operational_terms: classical record; entanglement-breaking channel; quantum memory; process hierarchy
page_or_section: pp. 2-3 Definition 1 Eqs. 6-7; pp. 4-7 Definition 3 Theorem 1 Table 1
specific_result_or_argument: For three or more times different physical memory mechanisms generate distinct classes that collapse in simpler two-time views.
admissible_interventions: conditional multi-time instruments
resource_bound: three or more times; realizability conditions
assumptions: declared multi-time process and carrier model
boundary_conditions: Two-time data are insufficient for the full hierarchy
alternative_interpretation: Non-Markovianity alone does not establish quantum or organizational memory
notes: Gives ICP a candidate carrier taxonomy while ruling out a single memory label.

claim_text: Full three-time process tomography on superconducting hardware detects temporal correlations and a quantum contribution to correlated noise beyond a Markov product model.
operational_terms: multi-time tomography; relative entropy; temporal negativity
page_or_section: pp. 1-3 protocol; pp. 4-5 Eq. 5 Eq. 6 Table 1; pp. 5-6 negativity test
specific_result_or_argument: Sequential informationally complete measure-and-prepare operations reconstruct a three-time Choi process on in-house and IBM devices.
admissible_interventions: measure-and-prepare sequence basis
observable_algebra: reconstructed operation span and final measurement
resource_bound: 324 sequences; stable device assumption; finite sampling
assumptions: SPAM treatment and process stationarity over data collection
boundary_conditions: Specific superconducting devices and three-time horizon
alternative_interpretation: Correlated noise can be diagnosed without identifying an ICP-level inherited organization
notes: Strong empirical example of history-dependent operational statistics.

claim_text: Process tomography does not uniquely identify the microscopic carrier and scales poorly with times and system size.
operational_terms: carrier underdetermination; SPAM; exponential scaling
specific_result_or_argument: The reconstructed process certifies temporal structure in an operational span but several environmental mechanisms can realize it.
admissible_interventions: implemented measure-and-prepare operations
resource_bound: exponential reconstruction cost and stability requirements
assumptions: valid process reconstruction within error
boundary_conditions: Device-specific boundary and limited horizon
alternative_interpretation: Operational memory may be real while the proposed physical embodiment remains unidentified
notes: Prevents overclaiming the physical identity of M.

claim_text: The observable redundantly recorded in an environment need not be unique across arbitrary environment decompositions.
operational_terms: redundant imprint; environment partition; comparable partitions; semi-GHZ
page_or_section: pp. 1-2 Eqs. 1-2; p. 2 comparable-partition condition; p. 3 uniqueness result
specific_result_or_argument: The same global state can encode redundant records of noncommuting observables under different factorizations; restricted comparable partitions restore uniqueness.
admissible_interventions: local measurements on environmental fragments
resource_bound: access to fragments and factorization choice
assumptions: global-state and redundancy definitions
boundary_conditions: Environment tensor factorization and comparability conditions
alternative_interpretation: Record objectivity is partition-relative and does not itself imply causal effect on future dynamics
notes: Boundary result for pillar 2 and for any intrinsic-carrier claim.

claim_text: Computational-mechanics causal states group histories with identical conditional distributions over the full observational future and are minimal optimal predictors.
operational_terms: causal state; predictive equivalence; epsilon-machine; statistical complexity
page_or_section: Definition 5 Eq. 16; Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 Eqs. 21-23; Theorems 2-3 Eqs. 26-27
specific_result_or_argument: The causal-state statistic is prescient minimal among equally predictive rivals and unique up to isomorphism under stated conditions.
admissible_interventions: passive observation histories
resource_bound: stationarity discrete alphabet and exact process law in main development
assumptions: stationary discrete-time stochastic process and measure-zero qualifications
boundary_conditions: Selected variables alphabet and predictive target
alternative_interpretation: Minimal predictive state is a statistic and need not be a localized physical carrier
notes: Clearest formal H-to-M-to-P(F|M) mapping.

claim_text: Predictive sufficiency does not by itself establish that a causal state is physically embodied or causally active.
operational_terms: predictive statistic; physical carrier; intervention
page_or_section: Sec. VII.B pp. 19-20; interpretation of definitions and theorems
specific_result_or_argument: The formal results concern equivalence of future conditional distributions; they do not supply a carrier intervention or a Pearl-style causal model.
admissible_interventions: none beyond observation in the base framework
assumptions: no additional embodiment theorem is imported
boundary_conditions: Observer-selected process representation
alternative_interpretation: Causal states can be epistemically sufficient summaries
notes: Connects to rival R005.

claim_text: Predictive information is the mutual information between past and future observation windows and equals the subextensive part of block entropy under the stated stationary setting.
operational_terms: predictive information; block entropy; mutual information
specific_result_or_argument: The measure distinguishes finite logarithmic and power-law growth regimes of learnable structure.
admissible_interventions: passive observation
resource_bound: finite windows and asymptotic model assumptions
assumptions: stationarity for block-entropy identities
boundary_conditions: Chosen observational process and model class
alternative_interpretation: Mutual information can arise from correlation without a manipulable carrier and says nothing alone about hard reachability
notes: A useful quantity but not an ICP principle.

claim_text: Once observables and resolution are chosen objective dynamics can determine a maximal predictive macrostate refinement.
operational_terms: macrostate; observable map; causal-state refinement; predictive efficiency
page_or_section: Secs. II-III; Sec. III.4; Secs. IV.1-IV.2
specific_result_or_argument: Causal states of selected macro-observations produce a sufficient Markovian predictive description consistent with the microdynamics.
admissible_interventions: passive observation and chosen coarse-graining
assumptions: Markov microdynamics and observation map
boundary_conditions: Question observable resolution and scale
alternative_interpretation: Emergent macrostates are objective only relative to a subjective measurement choice
notes: Offers a disciplined but explicitly relative macrostate construction.

claim_text: Apparent memory in a coarse variable can disappear when omitted state variables are added.
operational_terms: state augmentation; coarse-graining; position and velocity
specific_result_or_argument: A position-only description can appear non-Markovian whereas adding velocity restores a Markov state description.
admissible_interventions: change of state representation
assumptions: availability of the omitted variable and correct enlarged dynamics
boundary_conditions: Representation-dependent memory
alternative_interpretation: Ordinary complete-state dynamics explains history dependence
notes: Direct rival R002 and criterion F006.

claim_text: Epsilon-transducer states are minimal predictive equivalence classes of input-output histories for every admissible future input sequence.
operational_terms: epsilon-transducer; input-output channel; controlled prediction
page_or_section: Sec. III Definitions 1-4; Sec. VI Eq. 51 Definition 8; Sec. IX Theorems 2-3
specific_result_or_argument: Joint input-output pasts are equivalent when they induce the same future-output law for all future inputs; minimality and uniqueness follow under the model assumptions.
admissible_interventions: future input sequences admitted by the channel
resource_bound: stationary ergodic discrete alphabets; anticipation-free total channel
assumptions: specified input process and channel semantics
boundary_conditions: Input distribution affects state occupancy and complexity
alternative_interpretation: This may already exhaust much of an intervention-indexed predictive-state proposal
notes: Important prior art for ICP novelty analysis.

claim_text: Conditioning a channel on a future input sequence is not automatically a surgical intervention or a unit-level counterfactual.
operational_terms: input conditioning; intervention; causal model
page_or_section: Scope of Secs. III and VI interpreted with S016
specific_result_or_argument: The transducer supplies input-indexed output laws but causal semantics depend on how inputs are physically assigned and on hidden common causes.
admissible_interventions: declared channel inputs
resource_bound: causal identification assumptions not supplied by the transducer alone
assumptions: no unmodeled input confounding if interventional language is used
boundary_conditions: Physical control architecture
alternative_interpretation: A structural causal model may be needed to justify do-language
notes: Do not overstate the epsilon-transducer as counterfactual machinery.

claim_text: Maximizing path entropy under singlet constraints yields an independent process and adding pair-transition constraints yields a Markov process.
operational_terms: Maximum Caliber; path entropy; singlet constraints; pair constraints
specific_result_or_argument: Specified path-statistic constraints determine the maximum-caliber trajectory distribution and reproduce Markov structure.
admissible_interventions: constraints entered by the analyst
resource_bound: finite paths and chosen sufficient statistics
assumptions: maximum-entropy inference principle
boundary_conditions: Discrete state space and imposed constraints
alternative_interpretation: Constraints on inference are not evidence of a physically embodied constraint mechanism
notes: Useful machinery for P(Gamma|C) but analogy-only for ontology.

claim_text: Projection onto selected macroscopic variables yields an exact reduced equation with memory kernels representing unresolved degrees of freedom.
operational_terms: projection operator; memory kernel; reduced dynamics
specific_result_or_argument: Non-Markovian reduced evolution follows from ordinary microscopic dynamics when variables are projected out.
admissible_interventions: choice of relevant-variable projection
assumptions: underlying microscopic dynamics and selected projection
boundary_conditions: Reduced description
alternative_interpretation: History dependence may be an omitted-variable artifact rather than a new physical principle
notes: Classic support for rival R002.

claim_text: Ordinary conditioning and causal intervention answer different questions and interventional identification requires structural assumptions.
operational_terms: conditioning; set/do intervention; causal graph; identification
page_or_section: Abstract and pp. 430-431; structural semantics and inference rules
specific_result_or_argument: The causal calculus distinguishes P(y|X=x) from the distribution after externally setting X and specifies graphical conditions for valid transformations.
admissible_interventions: surgical interventions encoded in a causal model
assumptions: valid causal graph or structural equations
boundary_conditions: Target population interventions and observed variables
alternative_interpretation: Alternative predictive futures do not identify what the same unit would do under another action
notes: ICP must reserve counterfactual for models that supply cross-intervention semantics.

notes: One of four independent rows supporting the provisional synthesis claim.

claim_text: The strongest shared formal motif is a history-indexed family of future laws relative to a declared intervention set not a universal scalar called information.

claim_text: The strongest shared formal motif is a history-indexed family of future laws relative to a declared intervention set not a universal scalar called information.

claim_text: The strongest shared formal motif is a history-indexed family of future laws relative to a declared intervention set not a universal scalar called information.

claim_text: Task possibility path support probability weighting and predictive equivalence are non-isomorphic objects unless an explicit bridge is proved.

claim_text: Task possibility path support probability weighting and predictive equivalence are non-isomorphic objects unless an explicit bridge is proved.

specific_result_or_argument: Causal-state equivalence preserves observational future laws but does not decide which transformations are constructor-possible.

assumptions: native definitions retained

claim_text: Constructor theory of probability derives decision-supporting weights under strong conditions but does not derive an objective stochastic law or the Born rule.
operational_terms: partition of unity; decision-supporting superinformation; unpredictability
page_or_section: Abstract and Sec. 1 pp. 1-4; Sec. 3 Eqs. 3.1-3.3; Sec. 7(d) Eq. 7.10 and pp. 24-25; Sec. 8
specific_result_or_argument: Under specified superinformation and rationality conditions numerical weights guide decisions as if probabilities; the author explicitly limits the result.
admissible_interventions: measurement and game operations admitted by the theory
resource_bound: substantial symmetry measurement and rationality assumptions
assumptions: decision-supporting superinformation theory
boundary_conditions: Not an empirical frequency law and not a general stochastic process
alternative_interpretation: A decision-equivalence representation may coexist with several physical probability interpretations
notes: Prevents ICP from importing P^pi(F|M) from constructor theory without an additional bridge.

claim_text: Possible constructor-theory tasks can be represented as a symmetric monoidal subcategory of relations induced within a chosen reference process theory.
operational_terms: process theory; task relation; constructor attribute; coarse-graining
page_or_section: Sec. 3 Definitions 3.1-3.3 Proposition 3.4; Sec. 4 Definition 4.2 Proposition 4.3; Sec. 5

assumptions: symmetric monoidal process-theory setting
boundary_conditions: Constructor identity under reuse and simultaneous use remains open in the paper
alternative_interpretation: Absent extra restrictive principles constructor language may be an exact redescription inside ordinary process theory
notes: The redescription implication is the ICP synthesis inference not the authors' explicit verdict.

claim_text: A current proponent-authored review describes existing constructor-theory experiments mainly as compatibility demonstrations and identifies discriminating tests as future work.
operational_terms: test; compatibility; discriminator; maturity

admissible_interventions: varies by reviewed proposal

assumptions: review is authored by framework proponents and is not peer reviewed
boundary_conditions: Status current to June 2026
alternative_interpretation: A research agenda is not independent validation
notes: Background only; not counted as independent support.

claim_text: A Zipf-like marginal does not identify its generating mechanism.
operational_terms: rank-count marginal; causal underdetermination; mechanism
evidence_type: theoretical derivation and explicit methodological warning
specific_result_or_argument: Simon derives a cumulative-advantage family and then warns that conformity to the resulting distribution gives little information about the underlying phenomenon because other mechanisms can yield it.
admissible_interventions: innovation and reinforcement policies in the model
assumptions: class-level reinforcement and innovation assumptions
boundary_conditions: Asymptotic distribution does not identify microdynamics
alternative_interpretation: Alternative growth processes can match the same marginal
notes: Foundational anti-inference result for Batch 02.

claim_text: A Zipf-like marginal does not identify its generating mechanism.
operational_terms: rank-count marginal; causal underdetermination; mechanism
specific_result_or_argument: Independent random characters plus a delimiter generate a coarse Zipf-law-like word-frequency relation without memory semantics or communicative optimization.
predictive_interventional_or_counterfact: predictive under an iid character law
admissible_interventions: character and delimiter probabilities
assumptions: independent characters and delimiter segmentation
boundary_conditions: Result is strongest for length classes and does not reproduce full real-text structure
alternative_interpretation: Marginal scaling can be a segmentation artifact
notes: A memory-free null is sufficient to block inference from slope to ICP.

claim_text: A Zipf-like marginal does not identify its generating mechanism.
operational_terms: rank-count marginal; causal underdetermination; mechanism
specific_result_or_argument: Broad latent-variable mixtures can yield Zipf-like multivariate state probabilities without parameter tuning to an intrinsic critical point.
admissible_interventions: conditioning or intervention on latent common input
observable_algebra: joint state probabilities and energy-entropy relation
assumptions: latent variable modulates many degrees of freedom
boundary_conditions: Some latent transformations do not produce the effect
alternative_interpretation: Apparent criticality may be pooled heterogeneity
notes: Direct rival to critical or history-inheritance interpretations.

claim_text: A Zipf-like marginal does not identify its generating mechanism.
operational_terms: rank-count marginal; causal underdetermination; mechanism
specific_result_or_argument: A history-dependent sample-space-reducing walk also produces Zipf and noisy variants produce a family of exponents.
admissible_interventions: noise and reset policy
assumptions: canonical reducing walk with reset
boundary_conditions: Constructed ordering and support restriction
alternative_interpretation: A genuinely history-dependent process can share the marginal of memory-free or mixture accounts
notes: Together with S021 and S024 proves mechanism nonuniqueness.

claim_text: Random typing is a necessary null but the tested random-text families do not reproduce the full rank structure of real English texts.
operational_terms: random typing; plateaus; vocabulary width; rank statistics
page_or_section: Abstract; Eqs. 2-4; Figs. 1-3; Rigorous Statistical Fitting
specific_result_or_argument: Across ten English texts the tested iid-character models produce plateaus humps and vocabulary-width discrepancies and are rejected by rank summary statistics even when character probabilities come from the target text.
admissible_interventions: character-probability and corpus-length controls
observable_algebra: rank histogram vocabulary size mean rank and rank variance
resource_bound: ten texts and tested random-text families
assumptions: simulated model matches observed text length and declared character probabilities
boundary_conditions: Does not reject every possible segmentation model
alternative_interpretation: Failure of a simple null is not evidence for a particular alternative
notes: Preserves random typing as an anti-inference example while rejecting overclaiming its empirical adequacy.

claim_text: A least-effort signal-referent optimization can produce Zipf scaling near a communicative phase transition and predicts correlated changes in ambiguity information and lexicon size.
operational_terms: speaker effort; hearer effort; association matrix; mutual information
specific_result_or_argument: The weighted speaker-hearer cost has a transition near lambda about 0.41 where the signal-frequency distribution is Zipf-like and mutual information and lexicon size change abruptly.
admissible_interventions: cost weight and referent distribution
observable_algebra: signal frequency ambiguity mutual information and lexicon size
resource_bound: binary association matrix uniform referents heuristic optimization
assumptions: toy communication game and equilibrium search
boundary_conditions: No physical formation or carrier model
alternative_interpretation: Scaling may be transition-specific tuning rather than historical inheritance
notes: ICP relevance depends on identifying and manipulating an embodied learned association structure.

claim_text: Conditioning on a relevant latent variable can weaken a pooled Zipf law and diagnose a mixture mechanism.
operational_terms: latent conditioning; mixture; PEEV; pooled distribution
specific_result_or_argument: The paper develops a variance-explained diagnostic and reports that pooled word frequencies can be Zipfian while most part-of-speech strata are not; candidate latent variables explain substantial energy variance in studied systems.
admissible_interventions: condition on part of speech stimulus or other latent proxy
observable_algebra: conditional state probabilities energy variance and PEEV
resource_bound: candidate latent variable must be broad and coherently modulating
assumptions: observed proxy adequately tracks the relevant latent condition
boundary_conditions: Residual scaling can reflect unmeasured mixture or another mechanism
alternative_interpretation: Latent common drive need not be an inherited record
notes: Preregistered latent conditioning is mandatory before an intrinsic criticality or ICP claim.

claim_text: Sample-space reduction makes a history-dependent prediction beyond the marginal: successor support should be nested directional and disrupted by order destruction.
operational_terms: reachable support; nestedness; directionality; reset
specific_result_or_argument: The canonical process permits only lower-ranked successors until reset; noise mixes reduction with unrestricted sampling and controls the power-law exponent.
admissible_interventions: noise rate reset and state interventions
observable_algebra: successor support occupation and path-length distributions
assumptions: known state ordering and reset mechanism
boundary_conditions: Real systems can loop expand and reopen options
alternative_interpretation: Zipf can arise from path-dependent restriction but does not prove that restriction
notes: Direct formal neighbor to ICP's counterfactual reachable-future language.

claim_text: Sample-space reduction makes a history-dependent prediction beyond the marginal: successor support should be nested directional and disrupted by order destruction.
operational_terms: reachable support; nestedness; directionality; sentence formation
specific_result_or_argument: The language application links word-frequency exponents to nested successor sets and reports loss of the reported relationship under reversed or randomized structural controls.
admissible_interventions: shuffle reverse and alter successor matrix
observable_algebra: word transitions nestedness sentence paths and frequency distribution
resource_bound: binary successor support estimated from ten books
assumptions: estimated transition support represents sentence formation
boundary_conditions: Grammar topic and corpus reuse can create nestedness without a distinct physical carrier
alternative_interpretation: Static grammar or topic hierarchy may explain the same nestedness
notes: Requires held-out sequential likelihood and carrier tests before being called ICP evidence.

claim_text: Maximum entropy can derive a power-law family from a chosen log-moment constraint but does not by itself identify a physical constraint or sequential mechanism.
operational_terms: maximum entropy; log moment; cutoff; inference constraint
page_or_section: Eqs. 1-7; finite support Eqs. 15-24; hybrid Eqs. 33-35

admissible_interventions: change declared constraints

alternative_interpretation: Analyst knowledge can be confused with an embodied system constraint
notes: Use only after independent evidence identifies a physical enforcement mechanism.

claim_text: Zipf state probabilities admit a critical-like energy-entropy interpretation with testable finite-size and perturbation consequences.

claim_text: Zipf state probabilities admit a critical-like energy-entropy interpretation with testable finite-size and perturbation consequences.

claim_text: Zipf state probabilities admit a critical-like energy-entropy interpretation with testable finite-size and perturbation consequences.

notes: Mandatory rival row for every criticality claim.

claim_text: Rank-count scaling count-frequency scaling and Heaps type-token growth are distinct estimands and finite discrete systems do not permit silent exponent conversion.
